title: Art & Culture
summary: Classical and folk dances, music and maestros, paintings and crafts, temple architecture, festivals and fairs, and India's UNESCO lists. SSC asks 1–2 culture questions in almost every shift. Nearly all are pairings: dance–state, artist–instrument, craft–state or festival–state. The tables below cover almost all of them.

subtopics.title: Classical Dances & Their Exponents
subtopics.concept:
**Basics you must know:** The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** recognises **8 classical dances**. The Ministry of Culture also lists **Chhau** as classical, which makes 9.

| Dance | State | Signature points | Famous exponents |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Bharatanatyam** | Tamil Nadu | Oldest; temple *devadasi* roots; *Natya Shastra* based | **Rukmini Devi Arundale** (founded **Kalakshetra**, 1936), Padma Subrahmanyam, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Mrinalini Sarabhai |
| **Kathak** | Uttar Pradesh / north India | Only classical dance linked with the **Mughal courts**; *chakkars* (spins) and *tatkar* (footwork); Lucknow, Jaipur & Banaras gharanas | **Pt. Birju Maharaj**, Sitara Devi, Shovana Narayan |
| **Kathakali** | **Kerala** | Dance-drama; heavy make-up — green *pacha* for noble roles; Ramayana/Mahabharata stories | **Vallathol Narayana Menon** (founded **Kerala Kalamandalam**, 1930), Kalamandalam Gopi |
| **Mohiniyattam** | Kerala | Solo, graceful "dance of the enchantress" (Mohini) | Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, Bharati Shivaji |
| **Kuchipudi** | **Andhra Pradesh** | Named after **Kuchipudi village (Krishna district)**; **Tarangam** — dancing on the rim of a brass plate | **Vempati Chinna Satyam**, Raja & Radha Reddy |
| **Odissi** | Odisha | *Tribhanga* posture; temple sculpture roots (Konark) | **Kelucharan Mohapatra**, Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi |
| **Manipuri** | Manipur | **Ras Lila** of Radha–Krishna; soft, no ankle bells | **Guru Bipin Singh**, Jhaveri sisters |
| **Sattriya** | Assam | Created by **Sankardeva** (15th–16th c.) in the sattras; recognised in **2000** | Guru Jatin Goswami |

**Chhau** (Seraikela – Jharkhand, Mayurbhanj – Odisha, Purulia – West Bengal; masks used in Seraikela & Purulia) is on UNESCO's ICH list (2010).

tricks.title: Kerala has two, the rest one each
tricks.body: **K**erala = **K**athakali + Mohiniyattam. Every other classical dance has one home state: TN-Bharatanatyam, AP-Kuchipudi, Odisha-Odissi, Manipur-Manipuri, Assam-Sattriya, UP-Kathak.

example.q: Which state is home to two of the eight classical dances?
example.solution: **Kerala** — Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

tricks.title: Exponent hooks
tricks.body: **B**irju = **B**ol of Kathak · **K**elucharan = Odissi (**K**onark poses) · **R**ukmini Devi = **R**evived Bharatanatyam (Kalakshetra) · **V**empati = **V**illage Kuchipudi · **V**allathol = Kerala Kalamandalam (Kathakali).

mistakes: Kuchipudi is from **Andhra Pradesh**, not Tamil Nadu.
Mohiniyattam (Kerala) ≠ Manipuri (Manipur) — both are 'M' dances.
SNA lists **8** classical dances; 9 only if Chhau is counted (Ministry of Culture).
subtopics.notes:
### The nine classical dances
The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** recognises **8 classical dances**; the Ministry of Culture adds **Chhau** (making 9). Every dance is tied to one state — that pair is the core of the question.

| Dance | State | Signature | One famous name |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bharatanatyam | Tamil Nadu | Temple (devadasi) roots; oldest | Rukmini Devi Arundale |
| Kathak | UP / north | Mughal courts; chakkars, tatkar | Pt. Birju Maharaj |
| Kathakali | Kerala | Dance-drama; green (pacha) make-up | Kalamandalam Gopi |
| Mohiniyattam | Kerala | Lasya (graceful) solo of women | Sunanda Nair |
| Kuchipudi | Andhra Pradesh | Village Kuchipudi; plate (tarangam) balance | Raja & Radha Reddy |
| Odissi | Odisha | Tribhanga pose; temple dance of Jagannath | Kelucharan Mohapatra |
| Manipuri | Manipur | Raslila themes; soft, rounded movements | Jhaveri sisters |
| Sattriya | Assam | Sankaradeva's Vaishnava monasteries (sattra) | Indira P.P. Bora |
| Chhau | Odisha / Jharkhand / WB | Semi-classical martial dance | — |

Two Kerala dances and one UP dance — "Kerala has two" is the planted confusion: **Kathakali and Mohiniyattam** are Kerala; **Kathak** is the north Indian court dance.

### Exponents and revival
- **Rukmini Devi Arundale** — pulled Bharatanatyam out of its devadasi stigma and founded **Kalakshetra (1936)** at Chennai.
- **Vallathol Narayana Menon** — founded **Kerala Kalamandalam (1930)** to revive Kathakali.
- **Pt. Birju Maharaj** — Kathak of the **Lucknow gharana**; Sitara Devi was its celebrated 'Kathak queen'.
- **Kelucharan Mohapatra** — carried Odissi to the world stage.
- **Sonal Mansingh** — Odissi; Padma Vibhushan.

### Feature clues
Make-up and movement identify the dance faster than any list. **Kathakali**: elaborate green face (pacha = noble hero), codified hand language, drum-heavy. **Mohiniyattam**: white kasavu costume, lasya grace — 'the enchantress'. **Manipuri**: circular, flowing, never sharp — raslila of Radha-Krishna. **Odissi**: the **tribhanga** (three-bend) stance. **Kathak**: spinning chakkars and rhythmic footwork (tatkar), both Hindu and Mughal themes. **Sattriya**: the only classical dance born inside a monastery tradition, from **Srimanta Sankaradeva's** 15th-century Bhakti movement. **Kuchipudi**: male Brahmin theatre originally, by **Siddhendra Yogi's** codification; dancers often balance on a brass plate.

### The Chhau triangle
**Chhau** is a semi-classical masked/martial dance with three regional styles: **Mayurbhanj (Odisha — no masks)**, **Seraikella (Jharkhand — masks)** and **Purulia (West Bengal — masks)**. It entered the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in **2010**.

### Quick revision
- SNA: 8 classical; +Chhau = 9. Kerala: Kathakali + Mohiniyattam; UP: Kathak.
- Bharatanatyam—TN; Kuchipudi—AP; Odissi—Odisha; Manipuri—Manipur; Sattriya—Assam.
- Rukmini Devi = Kalakshetra 1936; Vallathol = Kalamandalam 1930.
- Odissi = tribhanga; Kathak = chakkars; Sattriya = sattra/Sankaradeva.
- Chhau: Mayurbhanj (no mask), Seraikella + Purulia (masks); UNESCO ICH 2010.

patterns.logic: Map clue to dance: green make-up = Kathakali; tribhanga = Odissi; raslila = Manipuri; plate balance = Kuchipudi; chakkars = Kathak; lasya = Mohiniyattam; sattra origin = Sattriya.

example.solution: **Odissi**, the temple dance of Odisha.

patterns.name: Institutions and recognition
patterns.howToSpot: 'Kalakshetra was founded by', 'Kerala Kalamandalam year', or when a dance got classical status.
patterns.logic: Two revivals to memorise: Kerala Kalamandalam (Vallathol, 1930) for Kathakali; Kalakshetra (Rukmini Devi Arundale, 1936) for Bharatanatyam. Sattriya got classical recognition in 2000.

example.q: **Kalakshetra**, the famous arts institution, was founded in 1936 by —
example.solution: **Rukmini Devi Arundale**, at Chennai, for Bharatanatyam.

subtopics.notes:
### Folk dances by state — the core table
| State | Dances (most asked in **bold**) |
|---|---|
| Gujarat | **Garba** (UNESCO ICH 2023), **Dandiya Raas**, Tippani |
| Rajasthan | **Ghoomar**, **Kalbelia** (ICH 2010), Chari, Kachchhi Ghodi |
| Punjab | **Bhangra** (men), **Giddha** (women) |
| Maharashtra | **Lavani**, Dhangari Gaja |
| Karnataka | **Yakshagana** (dance-drama) |
| Kerala | **Theyyam** (ritual), Ottam Thullal |
| Assam | **Bihu** |
| Mizoram | **Cheraw** (bamboo dance) |
| Tripura | **Hojagiri** (Reang balancing feats) |
| Meghalaya | **Nongkrem** (Khasi), Wangala (Garo) |
| Chhattisgarh | Karma, Panthi |
| Jharkhand | Karma, Chhau (Saraikela) |
| West Bengal | Chhau (Purulia) |

The North-East cluster (Cheraw–Hojagiri–Nongkrem) is a favourite match-the-column set: bamboo = Mizoram, balancing = Tripura, Khasi = Meghalaya.

### Feature and occasion clues
**Garba** — a circular women's dance of Navratri with clapping; **Dandiya Raas** uses sticks. **Ghoomar** — Bhil-origin, adopted by Rajasthan's royal houses, women in swirling ghagras. **Kalbelia** — of the snake-charmer Kalbelia community; imitative serpent movements; UNESCO ICH **2010**. **Bhangra/Giddha** — Baisakhi harvest. **Lavani** — fast tempo, dholki accompaniment, grown inside the **tamasha** theatre of Maharashtra. **Yakshagana** — Karnataka's night-long dance-drama with huge headgear; don't confuse it with Kathakali (Kerala). **Theyyam** — Kerala ritual where performers embody village goddesses, mostly male performers. **Bihu** — spring (Rongali) festival dance of Assam. **Cheraw** — dancers step between crossed bamboo staves clapped in rhythm. **Hojagiri** — Reang women balancing on pots and bottles. **Nongkrem** — Khasi thanksgiving dance. **Karma** — Karma-devi tree worship dance of Chhattisgarh-Jharkhand belt.

### The classical-folk border
**Chhau** sits on the border — semi-classical, martial, with three styles (Mayurbhanj, Seraikella, Purulia). **Yakshagana** is a folk dance-drama, not a classical dance. **Jatra** (Bengal) is folk theatre, not a dance. Exam setters swap these with classical names, so the state dance must be pinned before answering.

### Recognition to remember
- **Garba** — inscribed on UNESCO's ICH list in **2023** (India's newest dance element then).
- **Kalbelia, Chhau, Mudiyettu** — all inscribed in **2010**.
- **Durga Puja of Kolkata** (a festival, not a dance) — ICH **2021**.

### Quick revision
- Gujarat: Garba (ICH 2023) + Dandiya; Rajasthan: Ghoomar + Kalbelia (ICH 2010).
- Punjab: Bhangra/Giddha; Maharashtra: Lavani (tamasha); Karnataka: Yakshagana.
- Cheraw = Mizoram bamboo; Hojagiri = Tripura balancing; Nongkrem = Meghalaya Khasi.
- Theyyam = Kerala ritual; Bihu = Assam spring; Karma = Chhattisgarh-Jharkhand.
- 2010 ICH trio: Kalbelia, Chhau, Mudiyettu.

subtopics.title: Music, Instruments & Maestros
subtopics.concept:
**Two systems:** **Hindustani** (north; Persian influence; ragas tied to time of day; forms — *dhrupad* (oldest), *khayal*, *thumri*, *tappa*) and **Carnatic** (south; *kriti* composition; fixed compositions).

**Carnatic essentials**
- **Purandara Dasa** = "father (Pitamaha) of Carnatic music".
- **Trinity of Carnatic music:** **Tyagaraja**, **Muthuswami Dikshitar**, **Syama Sastri** (all 18th–19th c., Thiruvarur region, TN).
- **Tyagaraja Aradhana** festival is held at **Thiruvaiyaru**.

**Instrument → maestro**

| Instrument | Type | Maestro(s) |
|---|---|---|
| **Sitar** | String | **Pt. Ravi Shankar** (Bharat Ratna 1999), Vilayat Khan, Anoushka Shankar |
| Sarod | String | Ali Akbar Khan, Amjad Ali Khan |
| **Shehnai** | Wind | **Ustad Bismillah Khan** (Bharat Ratna 2001) |
| **Tabla** | Drum | **Zakir Hussain**, Alla Rakha, Kishan Maharaj |
| **Bansuri (flute)** | Wind | **Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia**, Pannalal Ghosh |
| Santoor | String (struck) | Shivkumar Sharma, Rahul Sharma |
| Sarangi | Bowed string | **Pt. Ram Narayan**, Sabri Khan |
| Violin (Carnatic) | Bowed | Lalgudi Jayaraman, L. Subramaniam, N. Rajam (Hindustani) |
| Mandolin | String | U. Srinivas |
| Mridangam | Drum | Palghat Mani Iyer, Umayalpuram Sivaraman |
| Veena (Saraswati) | String | E. Gayathri, S. Balachander |

**Vocalists who won the Bharat Ratna:** **M.S. Subbulakshmi (1998, first musician)**, Pt. Ravi Shankar (1999, sitar), Lata Mangeshkar (2001), Bismillah Khan (2001), **Pt. Bhimsen Joshi (2009, Kirana gharana)**, Bhupen Hazarika (2019, posthumous).

**Classical instrument families (Natya Shastra):** *Tata* (string) · *Sushira* (wind) · *Avanaddha* (membrane/drum) · *Ghana* (solid — cymbals, ghatam).

tricks.title: Carnatic Trinity — "Tea, Milk, Sugar"
tricks.body: **T**yagaraja · **M**uthuswami Dikshitar · **S**yama Sastri. **Purandara Dasa** is the *father*, not part of the trinity.

example.q: Who is called the Pitamaha of Carnatic music?
example.solution: **Purandara Dasa** — father, not one of the trinity.

tricks.title: Instrument families — "Tata Sings, Avan Drums, Ghana Clangs"
tricks.body: Tata = strings, Sushira = air (wind), Avanaddha = skin drums, Ghana = solid (bells, cymbals, ghatam).

mistakes: Sarod ≠ sitar: Ravi Shankar = **sitar**; Ali Akbar Khan & Amjad Ali Khan = **sarod**.
First musician to receive the Bharat Ratna = **M.S. Subbulakshmi (1998)**, not Lata Mangeshkar (2001).
Hariprasad Chaurasia plays the **flute**; Shivkumar Sharma played the **santoor**.
subtopics.notes:
### Two systems of classical music
**Hindustani** (north) — Persian influence; ragas tied to the time of day; older form *dhrupad*, then *khayal*, *thumri*, *tappa*; musicians belong to **gharanas**. **Carnatic** (south) — *kriti* compositions; the **Trinity: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri**; **Purandara Dasa** is the 'father (Pitamaha) of Carnatic music'. **Tansen**, at Akbar's court (one of the Navaratnas), is the fountainhead of Hindustani music.

### Instruments — the four-fold classification
| Class | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Tat** (stringed) | strings vibrated | sitar, veena, sarod, santoor, violin |
| **Sushir** (wind) | air column | flute (bansuri), shehnai, nadaswaram |
| **Avanaddha** (membrane) | skin struck | tabla, mridangam, pakhawaj, dholak |
| **Ghana** (solid) | struck/struck solid | ghatam, kanjira, manjira, jal tarang |

Quick sort: **shehnai = wind**, **santoor = stringed** (100 strings struck with mallets), **tabla = membranophone**, **ghatam = clay-pot idiophone**.

### Maestros ↔ instruments
| Maestro | Instrument |
|---|---|
| Ustad Bismillah Khan | Shehnai (Bharat Ratna 2001) |
| Pt. Ravi Shankar | Sitar (Bharat Ratna 1999) |
| Ustad Amjad Ali Khan / Ali Akbar Khan | Sarod |
| Ustad Zakir Hussain | Tabla |
| Pt. Shivkumar Sharma | Santoor |
| Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia | Flute |
| Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt | Mohan veena (slide guitar) |
| Ustad Allah Rakha | Tabla (Zakir's father) |
| M.S. Subbulakshmi | Carnatic vocal (first musician Bharat Ratna, 1998) |
| Pt. Bhimsen Joshi | Hindustani vocal (Kirana gharana; Bharat Ratna 2008) |
| Ustad Allauddin Khan | Sarod/raga architect — Maihar gharana; teacher of Ravi Shankar and Ali Akbar Khan |

**M.S. Subbulakshmi** (1998) was the **first musician** to get the Bharat Ratna; Ravi Shankar followed in 1999. Lata Mangeshkar (2001) and Bhimsen Joshi (2008) complete the musician Bharat Ratnas.

### Gharanas (Hindustani)
**Gwalior** is the oldest khayal gharana. Others: **Kirana** (Bhimsen Joshi's line via Abdul Karim Khan), **Jaipur-Atrauli**, **Agra**, **Patiala** (Bade Ghulam Ali Khan), **Banaras** (tabla and thumri). Tabla gharanas: Lucknow, Farrukhabad, Banaras, Punjab, Delhi. In Kathak, gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

### The violin in Carnatic music
The European violin was absorbed into Carnatic music around the 18th–19th century (credited to **Baluswami Dikshitar**, brother of Muthuswami); it is now indispensable as an accompaniment. The **nadaswaram** (wind) leads temple processions in the south, paired with the **thavil** drum.

### Quick revision
- Purandara Dasa = Carnatic Pitamaha; Trinity = Tyagaraja, Dikshitar, Syama Sastri.
- Tat-sushir-avanaddha-ghana: sitar-shehnai-tabla-ghatam.
- Bismillah Khan = shehnai (BR 2001); Ravi Shankar = sitar (BR 1999); MS 1998 = first musician BR.
- Shivkumar Sharma = santoor; Chaurasia = flute; Zakir Hussain = tabla.
- Gwalior = oldest gharana; Allauddin Khan = Maihar.

patterns.name: Instrument ↔ class
patterns.howToSpot: 'Shehnai is what kind of instrument', or odd-one-out among wind/string/percussion instruments.
patterns.logic: Use the four classes: tat (stringed), sushir (wind), avanaddha (membrane drum), ghana (solid). Flute/shehnai/nadaswaram = wind; tabla/mridangam = drum; ghatam/kanjira = solid; sitar/sarod/santoor = string.

example.q: The **shehnai** is classified as —
example.solution: A **wind (sushir) instrument** — sound from a vibrating air column.

patterns.name: Maestro ↔ instrument
patterns.howToSpot: A musician's name (Bismillah Khan, Zakir Hussain, Shivkumar Sharma…) with four instruments.
patterns.logic: One-to-one map: Bismillah Khan-shehnai, Ravi Shankar-sitar, Amjad Ali Khan/Ali Akbar Khan-sarod, Zakir Hussain/Allah Rakha-tabla, Shivkumar Sharma-santoor, Chaurasia-flute, Vishwa Mohan Bhatt-mohan veena.

example.q: Ustad **Zakir Hussain** is a virtuoso of —
example.solution: The **tabla** — son of the legendary Ustad Allah Rakha.

patterns.name: Hindustani vs Carnatic
patterns.howToSpot: 'Father of Carnatic music', the Carnatic Trinity, Tansen's court, or a statement-pair about the two systems.
patterns.logic: North = Hindustani (dhrupad/khayal, gharanas, Tansen); South = Carnatic (kriti, Trinity, Purandara Dasa). Any 'Pitamaha' question points to Purandara Dasa.

example.q: The **Carnatic Trinity** consists of —
example.solution: **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri**.

patterns.name: Bharat Ratna musicians & gharanas
patterns.howToSpot: 'First musician to get the Bharat Ratna', which gharana a singer belongs to, the oldest gharana.
patterns.logic: Order of musician Bharat Ratnas: M.S. Subbulakshmi (1998), Ravi Shankar (1999), Lata Mangeshkar (2001), Bismillah Khan (2001), Bhimsen Joshi (2008). Gwalior = oldest khayal gharana; Maihar = Allauddin Khan's school.

example.q: Who was the **first musician** to be awarded the Bharat Ratna?
example.solution: **M.S. Subbulakshmi** (1998) — the Carnatic vocalist.

subtopics.notes:
### Folk and tribal paintings → state
| Painting | State | Hallmark |
|---|---|---|
| **Madhubani (Mithila)** | **Bihar** | Women's wall art; double-line work; GI tag |
| **Warli** | Maharashtra | White rice-paste stick figures on mud walls |
| **Pattachitra** | Odisha (also WB) | Cloth/palm-leaf scrolls of Jagannath iconography |
| **Phad** | Rajasthan | Long cloth scrolls of Pabuji/Devnarayan epics |
| **Kalamkari** | Andhra Pradesh / Telangana | Pen-drawn (Srikalahasti) or block-printed (Machilipatnam) |
| **Gond** | Madhya Pradesh | Tribal dot-and-dash pattern painting |
| **Thangka** | Ladakh / Sikkim | Buddhist cloth scrolls used in worship |
| **Cheriyal** | Telangana | Brightly coloured story scrolls |
| **Pichwai** | Rajasthan (Nathdwara) | Backdrop paintings of Srinathji (Krishna) |

### Miniature schools
**Mughal** painting — founded under **Akbar** (*Hamzanama* workshops), peaked under **Jahangir** (portraits, naturalism). **Rajasthani** schools (Mewar, Kishangarh — the Bani-Thani style). **Pahari** schools of the Himalayan foothills — **Kangra** is the most celebrated, with Radha-Krishna themes. **Company paintings** (late 18th–19th c.) were made for British patrons. The **Bengal School** — **Abanindranath Tagore** (his *Bharat Mata*, 1905), backed by E.B. Havell and carried by **Nandalal Bose** — answered Western academic style with an Asian idiom. **Raja Ravi Varma** — Kerala's oil painter who fused European realism with Indian subjects through mass lithographs.

### Crafts ↔ place
| Craft | Place |
|---|---|
| **Bidriware** (silver on blackened alloy) | Bidar, Karnataka |
| **Pochampally ikat** | Telangana |
| **Kanjeevaram silk** | Tamil Nadu |

| **Phulkari** (flower work) | Punjab |
| **Channapatna lacquer toys** | Karnataka |
| **Blue pottery** | Jaipur |
| **Pashmina** shawls | Kashmir |
| **Brass ware** | Moradabad, UP |

### Memory hooks
Wall-women-Mithila = Madhubani (Bihar). White-on-mud = Warli. Jagannath scroll = Pattachitra. Silver-on-black = Bidri. Tie-dye = Bandhani. Kalamkari literally = pen-work (kalam = pen). Nathdwara backdrop = Pichwai.

- Mughal: Akbar founds (Hamzanama), Jahangir peaks; Kangra = Pahari gem.
- Bengal School: Abanindranath Tagore (Bharat Mata 1905), Nandalal Bose.
- Bidri-Bidar; Chikankari-Lucknow; Phulkari-Punjab; Pochampally-Telangana.

**Three temple styles**

| **Vesara** | Deccan (Karnataka) | Mix of Nagara & Dravida; star-shaped plans | **Hoysala** temples of Belur, Halebidu, Somnathapura; later Chalukya temples |

**Odisha temples:** **Konark Sun Temple** — **Narasimhadeva I (Eastern Ganga)**, 13th c., chariot with 24 wheels, "Black Pagoda", UNESCO 1984. **Jagannath Temple, Puri** — Anantavarman Chodaganga, "White Pagoda". Lingaraja, Bhubaneswar.

subtopics.notes:
### The three temple styles
| Style | Region | Hallmark | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Nagara** | North | Curvilinear **shikhara** over the sanctum; **amalaka** on top; no boundary wall | Khajuraho (Chandela), Konark, Lingaraja (Bhubaneswar), Modhera Sun Temple |
| **Dravida** | South | Pyramid **vimana**, towering **gopuram** gateways, enclosed courts | Brihadeeswara (Thanjavur), Meenakshi (Madurai), Srirangam |
| **Vesara** | Deccan | Hybrid of the two | Chalukya (Pattadakal, Badami), **Hoysala** (Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura) |

Feature sort: **shikhara** = north's curving tower; **vimana** = the south's pyramidal tower **above the sanctum**; **gopuram** = the monumental gateway of south temples; **mandapa** = pillared hall.

### Monument ↔ builder
| Monument | Builder / period |
|---|---|
| Brihadeeswara, Thanjavur (Rajrajeswara) | **Rajaraja I**, Chola (c. 1010 CE) |
| Gangaikonda Cholapuram | **Rajendra I**, Chola |
| **Sun Temple, Konark** | **Narasimhadeva I**, Eastern Ganga (13th c.) |
| Sun Temple, Modhera | **Bhima I**, Solanki (Chaulukya) |
| Kailasa temple, Ellora (rock-cut) | **Krishna I**, Rashtrakuta |
| Chennakesava, Belur | **Vishnuvardhana**, Hoysala (1117) |
| Hoysaleswara, Halebidu | Hoysala kings |
| Kesava, Somanathapura | Hoysala (Narasimha III's reign, 1268) |
| Dilwara Jain temples, Mt Abu | Solanki period (Vimal Shah's Vimal Vasahi) |
| Meenakshi temple, Madurai | Nayak rulers (gopurams restored/expanded) |
| Mahabalipuram rathas & Shore Temple | **Pallavas** — Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) and Rajasimha |

### Rock-cut caves
**Ajanta** — Buddhist, painted frescoes (Bodhisattva Padmapani), two phases (Satavahana c. 2nd c. BCE; Vakataka 5th c. CE). **Ellora** — Buddhist-Hindu-Jain together; the **Kailasa** temple carved top-down from one rock under **Rashtrakuta Krishna I**. **Elephanta** — mid-first-millennium rock-cut Shiva (Maheshmurti) island caves near Mumbai. **Mahabalipuram** — Pallava monolithic **rathas** and the Shore Temple. **Chaitya** = prayer hall; **vihara** = monastery — the Buddhist cave pair (Karle chaitya, Ajanta viharas).

### Quick revision
- Nagara = shikhara (north); Dravida = vimana + gopuram (south); Vesara = hybrid (Deccan).
- Konark = Narasimhadeva I; Brihadeeswara = Rajaraja I; Modhera = Bhima I.
- Kailasa (Ellora) = Krishna I, Rashtrakuta — carved top-down.
- Belur/Halebidu/Somanathapura = Hoysala; Pattadakal = Chalukya (UNESCO 1987).
- Ajanta = Buddhist frescoes; chaitya = hall, vihara = monastery.

subtopics.notes:
### Festival ↔ state — the core table
| Festival | State | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Onam** | Kerala | King Mahabali's homecoming; Vallam Kali boat race; pookalam |
| **Pongal** | Tamil Nadu | Mid-January harvest; four days; Jallikattu |
| **Baisakhi** | Punjab | April harvest; Khalsa founding (1699) |
| **Bihu** | Assam | Rongali (spring) the famous one |
| **Durga Puja** | West Bengal | UNESCO ICH 2021 |
| **Ganesh Chaturthi** | Maharashtra | Public sarvajanik utsav (Tilak's mobilisation) |
| **Chhath** | Bihar / Jharkhand | Sun (Surya) worship at rivers, Kartik Shukla Shashthi |
| **Hornbill** | Nagaland | 1–10 December, Kisama; 'festival of festivals' |
| **Losar** | Ladakh / Arunachal | Tibetan new year |
| **Wangala** | Meghalaya | Garo harvest festival |
| **Sarhul** | Jharkhand | Tribal spring festival of the sal tree |
| **Makar Sankranti / Lohri** | Pan-India / Punjab | Lohri falls the night before Sankranti |

### Fairs (melas)
**Kumbh Mela** — rotates among **Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik** (UNESCO ICH 2017). **Pushkar** (Rajasthan) — Kartik Purnima camel and livestock fair at the only Brahma temple. **Sonepur** (Bihar) — one of Asia's largest cattle fairs at the Gandak-Ganga confluence. **Nauchandi** (Meerut, UP).

### Season logic
Most Indian festivals are harvest-tied: Pongal (mid-Jan, Tamil Thai month), Baisakhi (mid-April), Bihu (April), Onam (Aug–Sep, Chingam), Wangala (autumn). Winter-solstice cluster: Lohri → Makar Sankranti → Pongal → Bihu within a day or two.

### UNESCO ICH elements of India
**Kutiyattam** (Sanskrit theatre, 2001 — the first), **Ramlila** and the **Vedic chanting** tradition (2008), **Chhau, Kalbelia, Mudiyettu** (2010), **Sankirtana** of Manipur (2013), **Yoga** (2016), **Kumbh Mela** (2017), **Durga Puja in Kolkata** (2021), **Garba of Gujarat** (2023), **Ramman** (Garhwal, 2009 — festival-theatre).

### Two questions that repeat
1. **Which city does not host the Kumbh?** The four are Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik — Varanasi, Ayodhya and Mathura are the decoys.
2. **Which dance belongs to which festival?** Garba-Navratri, Bhangra-Baisakhi, Bihu-Rongali Bihu, Jallikattu-Pongal, Vallam Kali-Onam. Pair them and half the festival questions answer themselves.

### Quick revision
- Onam-Kerala (Mahabali, Vallam Kali); Pongal-TN (Jan); Baisakhi-Punjab (Khalsa 1699).
- Chhath = Bihar sun worship; Hornbill = Nagaland, Dec; Losar = Ladakh new year.
- Kumbh: Prayagraj-Haridwar-Ujjain-Nashik; Pushkar = camel fair; Sonepur = Bihar cattle.
- ICH ladder: Kutiyattam 2001 → Ramlila/Veda 2008 → Chhau-Kalbelia-Mudiyettu 2010 → Sankirtana 2013 → Yoga 2016 → Kumbh 2017 → Durga Puja 2021 → Garba 2023.

subtopics.notes:
### India's World Heritage Sites — the landscape
India holds **45 World Heritage Sites** (37 cultural, 7 natural, 1 mixed — **Khangchendzonga National Park**, Sikkim, 2016). The 1983 founding batch: **Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora**. Recent cultural inscriptions: **Ramappa (Rudreswara) Temple** and **Dholavira** (both 2021), **Santiniketan** and the **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas** (2023), the **Moidams** of Assam (2024), **Maratha Military Landscapes** (2025) and the **Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath** (2026). India's first city WHS is **Ahmedabad** (2017); Jaipur followed (2019).

### Natural and mixed sites
Natural: **Kaziranga, Manas, Keoladeo, Sundarbans** (East), **Nanda Devi**, **Western Ghats**, **Great Himalayan National Park**. Mixed: only **Khangchendzonga**.

### Cultural institutions
| Institution | Founded | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** | 1861 | Custodian of monuments; Alexander Cunningham first DG |
| **Sangeet Natak Akademi** | 1953 | Performing arts; New Delhi |
| **Sahitya Akademi** | 1954 | Literature |
| **Lalit Kala Akademi** | 1954 | Fine arts |
| **FTII** | 1960 | Film and Television Institute of India, Pune |
| **INTACH** | 1984 | Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage |
| **IGNCA** | 1987 | Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, New Delhi |

The three Akademis (Sangeet Natak, Sahitya, Lalit Kala) are the National Akademies set up in the 1950s — Sangeet Natak first (1953).

### Memory hooks
- 1983 = Taj + Agra Fort + Ajanta + Ellora (the first four).
- 2021 = Ramappa + Dholavira; 2023 = Santiniketan + Hoysala Ensembles.
- Mixed = Khangchendzonga only. Natural quartet of the East: Kaziranga, Manas, Keoladeo, Sundarbans.
- Akademis: Sangeet Natak 1953, Sahitya + Lalit Kala 1954; ASI 1861 (Cunningham).

### How the questions are built
Most WHS questions test one of three things: **the state** (Ramappa-Telangana, Dholavira-Gujarat, Santiniketan-Bengal, Hoysalas-Karnataka, Moidams-Assam), **the year** (the 2021 pair, the 2023 pair), or **the type** (mixed = Khangchendzonga, natural = the wildlife quartet). Institution questions test the **year and the art**: performing arts 1953, literature and fine arts 1954, films 1960, archaeology 1861. Learn each site as a triple — site + state + year — and every variant collapses into recall.

### Quick revision
- 45 WHS = 37 cultural + 7 natural + 1 mixed (Khangchendzonga).
- First four (1983): Taj, Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora.
- 2021: Ramappa (Telangana), Dholavira (Gujarat); 2023: Santiniketan, Hoysalas.
- ASI 1861 Cunningham; SNA 1953; Sahitya + Lalit Kala 1954; FTII 1960 Pune.

example.q: India's **first heritage city** on the WHS list is —

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A classical or folk dance named with four states as options (or a 'correctly matched pair' set).
pyqPatterns.approach: Classical nine first: TN-Bharatanatyam, UP-Kathak, Kerala-Kathakali + Mohiniyattam ('Kerala has two'), AP-Kuchipudi, Odisha-Odissi, Manipur-Manipuri, Assam-Sattriya. For folk, run the state table; NE dances fall to the mnemonic Cheraw-bamboo (Mizoram), Hojagiri-balancing (Tripura), Nongkrem-Khasi (Meghalaya).

example.q: **Kathakali** belongs to which state?
example.solution: **Kerala** — which also owns Mohiniyattam; Karnataka's dance-drama Yakshagana is folk, not classical.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A maestro's name (Birju Maharaj, Bismillah Khan, Zakir Hussain, Kelucharan Mohapatra) with four art forms.
pyqPatterns.approach: One-to-one pairs: Birju Maharaj-Kathak, Rukmini Devi-Bharatanatyam (Kalakshetra), Mohapatra-Odissi, Bismillah Khan-shehnai, Ravi Shankar-sitar, Amjad Ali Khan-sarod, Zakir Hussain-tabla, Shivkumar Sharma-santoor, Chaurasia-flute.

example.q: Ustad **Bismillah Khan** was a maestro of —
example.solution: The **shehnai** — Bharat Ratna 2001.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Madhubani, Warli, Pattachitra, Phad or a craft (Bidri, Chikankari) with four states/places.
pyqPatterns.approach: Big five paintings: Madhubani-Bihar, Warli-Maharashtra, Pattachitra-Odisha, Phad-Rajasthan, Gond-MP. Crafts: Bidriware-Bidar, Chikankari-Lucknow, Phulkari-Punjab, Pochampally-Telangana, Blue pottery-Jaipur.

example.q: **Warli** painting, with white stick figures on mud walls, is from —
example.solution: **Maharashtra** — tribal wall art of the Warli belt.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Onam, Pongal, Chhath, Hornbill, Bihu or a mela (Pushkar, Sonepur, Kumbh) with state options.
pyqPatterns.approach: Onam-Kerala, Pongal-TN, Baisakhi-Punjab, Bihu-Assam, Chhath-Bihar, Hornbill-Nagaland (Dec), Losar-Ladakh. Kumbh rotates Prayagraj-Haridwar-Ujjain-Nashik; Pushkar = camels, Sonepur = cattle.

example.q: The **Onam** harvest festival is celebrated in —
example.solution: **Kerala** — Mahabali's homecoming, with Vallam Kali boat races.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A recent WHS inscription and its state, or a temple (Konark, Brihadeeswara, Belur) with its builder/dynasty.
pyqPatterns.approach: Recent WHS: 2021 Ramappa-Telangana + Dholavira-Gujarat; 2023 Santiniketan-WB + Hoysala Ensembles-Karnataka; 2024 Moidams-Assam. Builders: Konark-Narasimhadeva I, Thanjavur-Rajaraja I, Belur-Vishnuvardhana, Kailasa-Krishna I.

example.q: The **Sun Temple at Konark** was built by —
example.solution: **Narasimhadeva I** of the Eastern Ganga dynasty (13th century).

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: A clue described in words — green make-up, tribhanga, raslila, plate balance, chakkars, bamboo — and the dance asked.
pyqPatterns.approach: Kathakali-green make-up; Odissi-tribhanga; Manipuri-raslila; Kuchipudi-plate (tarangam); Kathak-chakkars; Mohiniyattam-lasya; Sattriya-sattra; Cheraw-bamboo; Hojagiri-balancing.

example.q: Balancing on a **brass plate (tarangam)** identifies which classical dance?
example.solution: **Kuchipudi** (Andhra Pradesh).

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Kerala Kalamandalam was founded in', 'Kalakshetra by whom', 'which Akademi and when', 'ASI's first DG'.
pyqPatterns.approach: Culture bodies: Kalamandalam 1930 (Vallathol), Kalakshetra 1936 (Rukmini Devi), ASI 1861 (Cunningham), Sangeet Natak Akademi 1953, Sahitya + Lalit Kala 1954, FTII 1960 Pune.

example.q: **Kerala Kalamandalam** was founded in 1930 by —
example.solution: Poet **Vallathol Narayana Menon**, to revive Kathakali.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: An intangible element (Garba, Kalbelia, Durga Puja, Kumbh, Yoga) matched to its inscription year or home state.
pyqPatterns.approach: The ICH ladder: Kutiyattam 2001, Ramlila + Vedic chanting 2008, Ramman 2009, Chhau + Kalbelia + Mudiyettu 2010, Sankirtana 2013, Yoga 2016, Kumbh 2017, Durga Puja 2021, Garba 2023.

example.q: **Garba** entered the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in —
example.solution: **2023** — India's newest major dance element on the list.

solvedExamples.q: Which of the following classical dance–state pairs is **NOT** correctly matched?
solvedExamples.solution: **Kuchipudi** is from **Andhra Pradesh** (Kuchipudi village, Krishna district). Tamil Nadu's classical dance is Bharatanatyam. The other three pairs are correct.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Only Kerala has two classical dances; Tamil Nadu has just one (Bharatanatyam), so the Kuchipudi pair must be wrong.

solvedExamples.q: **Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia** is renowned as a player of the —
solvedExamples.solution: **Hariprasad Chaurasia** is India's best-known **bansuri** (bamboo flute) player (Padma Vibhushan 2000). Sitar – Ravi Shankar; sarangi – Ram Narayan; tabla – Zakir Hussain.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Chaurasia's 'Call of the Valley' pairs **flute** with Shivkumar Sharma's santoor.

solvedExamples.q: Which of the following is **NOT** on UNESCO's list of India's Intangible Cultural Heritage?
solvedExamples.solution: Yoga (2016), Kumbh Mela (2017) and Garba (2023) are inscribed. **Onam** is not on the list (India's festival entries are Ramman, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja and Deepavali).
solvedExamples.shortcut: Recall the 2016–2025 run: Yoga, Kumbh, Durga Puja, Garba, Deepavali — Onam is missing.

solvedExamples.q: The Ellora caves in Maharashtra contain rock-cut shrines of which religious traditions?
solvedExamples.solution: Ellora's **34 caves** (c. 6th–10th century) include 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu (including the Kailasa temple, Cave 16) and 5 Jain caves. Ajanta, by contrast, is purely Buddhist.

practice.q: **Kathakali**, the dance-drama known for its elaborate green face make-up, is a classical dance of —
practice.solution: **Kathakali** is from **Kerala**; the poet Vallathol founded Kerala Kalamandalam (1930) to revive it. Karnataka's comparable dance-drama is Yakshagana (a folk form).

practice.q: The classical dance **Kuchipudi** takes its name from a village in which state?
practice.solution: Kuchipudi village is in the **Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh**. The dance is known for *Tarangam*, performed on the rim of a brass plate.

practice.q: **Pandit Birju Maharaj** was a celebrated exponent of —
practice.solution: **Birju Maharaj** (1938–2022) of the **Lucknow (Kalka-Bindadin) gharana** was the leading figure of **Kathak** and received the Padma Vibhushan.

practice.q: **Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra** is associated with the revival of which dance?
practice.solution: **Kelucharan Mohapatra** (1926–2004) shaped modern **Odissi**; he was the first Odia to receive the Padma Vibhushan.

practice.q: **Garba**, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023, is a dance form of —
practice.solution: **Garba of Gujarat** is performed around a lamp (*garbo*) during Navratri. It became India's 15th ICH element in December 2023.

practice.q: **Cheraw**, the bamboo dance in which dancers step in and out of clapping bamboo poles, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Cheraw** is the traditional bamboo dance of **Mizoram**, often performed at Chapchar Kut. Tripura's well-known dance is Hojagiri.
practice.shortcut: NE five: **Cheraw Mizo**, Hoja Tripura, Nong Khasi, Wang Garo, Bagu Bodo.

practice.q: Which of the following is **NOT** one of the 'Trinity' of Carnatic music?
practice.solution: The Trinity is **Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri**. **Purandara Dasa** (16th century) is honoured as the *Pitamaha* (father) of Carnatic music.
practice.shortcut: Tea, Milk, Sugar = T, M, S — no 'P'.

practice.q: **Ustad Bismillah Khan**, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, was a maestro of the —
practice.solution: **Bismillah Khan** of Varanasi took the **shehnai** from wedding music to the concert stage and played it at the Red Fort on 15 August 1947.
practice.shortcut: Shehnai = wind instrument of Varanasi ghats = Bismillah.

practice.q: Who was the first musician to be awarded the **Bharat Ratna**?
practice.solution: Carnatic vocalist **M.S. Subbulakshmi** received the Bharat Ratna in **1998**. Ravi Shankar followed in 1999, Lata Mangeshkar in 2001 and Bhimsen Joshi in 2009.

practice.q: **Madhubani** painting, traditionally drawn by women of the Mithila region, belongs to —
practice.solution: Madhubani (Mithila) painting is from **Bihar**, marked by double-line borders and natural colours. It has a GI tag. Odisha's scroll art is Pattachitra.

practice.q: **Kalamkari**, the art of hand-painting or block-printing cotton textiles with natural dyes, is chiefly associated with —
practice.solution: Kalamkari ('pen-work') is practised at **Srikalahasti** (free-hand) and **Machilipatnam** (block-printed) in **Andhra Pradesh**.

practice.q: **Bidriware**, a metal craft with silver inlay on a blackened alloy, originated in —
practice.solution: Bidri work takes its name from **Bidar in Karnataka**, where it developed under the Bahmani sultans. Moradabad is known for brassware.
practice.shortcut: The craft carries its town's name: **Bidri** → **Bidar**.

practice.q: The **Sun Temple at Konark** was built by —
practice.solution: The Eastern Ganga king **Narasimhadeva I** built Konark in the 13th century as a giant chariot of the Sun god with 24 wheels. Anantavarman Chodaganga built the Jagannath temple at Puri; Kharavela is linked with the Hathigumpha inscription.

practice.q: Towering gateways called **gopurams** are a characteristic feature of which temple style?
practice.solution: In the **Dravida** style the sanctum is topped by a pyramidal **vimana**, and later temples have huge **gopurams** in the enclosure walls (e.g. Meenakshi temple, Madurai). Nagara temples have a curved shikhara and no gopuram.

practice.q: The **Hornbill Festival**, called the 'festival of festivals', is held every December in —
practice.solution: The Hornbill Festival is held from **1 to 10 December** at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, **Nagaland**, showcasing all Naga tribes.

practice.q: The **Sonepur Mela**, one of Asia's largest cattle fairs, is held at the confluence of the Gandak and the Ganga in —
practice.solution: Sonepur (Saran district, **Bihar**) hosts the fair from Kartik Purnima. Rajasthan's famous camel fair is at Pushkar.

practice.q: **Ramman**, a religious festival and ritual theatre inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2009, is performed in —
practice.solution: Ramman is performed in the Saloor-Dungra villages of **Chamoli district (Garhwal), Uttarakhand**, in honour of the local deity Bhumiyal Devta.
practice.shortcut: Ramman – Garhwal – Uttarakhand (2009, right after the 2008 first batch).

practice.q: The **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas**, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023, are located in —
practice.solution: The ensemble covers the Hoysala temples at **Belur, Halebidu and Somnathapura** in **Karnataka**. It became India's 42nd World Heritage Site.

practice.q: The classical dance **Kathakali** belongs to —
practice.solution: **Kathakali** is Kerala's story-dance; Vallathol founded Kerala Kalamandalam (1930) to revive it.

practice.q: **Mohiniyattam**, the 'dance of the enchantress', is a classical dance of —
practice.solution: **Mohiniyattam** — Kerala's graceful lasya solo; Kerala thus has two classical dances, Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.

practice.q: Which classical dance is associated with the state of **Assam**?
practice.solution: **Sattriya** was created by Srimanta Sankaradeva's Vaishnava tradition and preserved in the **sattra** monasteries of Assam.

practice.q: Which of the following is a classical dance of **North-East India** other than Sattriya?
practice.solution: **Manipuri** (Manipur) is classical — themed on the **raslila**; Bihu, Cheraw and Hojagiri are folk dances.

practice.q: The dancer **Kalamandalam Gopi** is a legendary performer of —
practice.solution: **Kalamandalam Gopi** — a stellar Kathakali artiste from the Kerala Kalamandalam tradition.

practice.q: **Raja and Radha Reddy** are renowned exponents of —
practice.solution: The **Reddy duo** carried Kuchipudi to world stages and run an academy in Delhi.

practice.q: **Sonal Mansingh**, a Padma Vibhushan dancer, is associated mainly with —
practice.solution: **Sonal Mansingh** — an Odissi (and Bharatanatyam) dancer, honoured with the Padma Vibhushan.

practice.q: The elaborate **green face make-up (pacha)** is characteristic of —
practice.solution: In Kathakali, **pacha (green)** marks noble characters; knife characters wear red, demons black.

practice.q: Balancing on a **brass plate (tarangam)** while dancing is a specialty of —
practice.solution: The **tarangam** — dancing on the rim of a brass plate, sometimes with a pot on the head — is a Kuchipudi showpiece.

practice.q: The **raslila** theme of Radha and Krishna is central to which classical dance?
practice.solution: **Manipuri** dance grew out of the Vaishnava raslila tradition of Manipur; its movements are soft and circular.

practice.q:
Match the pose/feature with the dance:
1. Chakkars (spins) — Kathak
2. Lasya grace — Mohiniyattam
3. Chauka stance — Odissi
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three are correct: Kathak's spins, Mohiniyattam's lasya, and Odissi's square **chauka** stance (alongside tribhanga).

practice.q: **Kerala Kalamandalam**, founded in 1930 to revive Kathakali, was set up by —
practice.solution: Poet **Vallathol Narayana Menon** founded Kalamandalam in 1930; Rukmini Devi's Kalakshetra came six years later.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Sattriya received classical dance status in 2000.
2. Chhau is on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list.
3. Kathak has three major gharanas — Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three hold: Sattriya was recognised classical in **2000**; Chhau entered the UNESCO ICH list in **2010**; Kathak's gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

practice.q: **Garba**, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023, is a folk dance of —
practice.solution: **Garba** is Gujarat's Navratri circle dance; it entered the UNESCO ICH list in **2023**.

practice.q: **Bhangra** and **Giddha** are folk dances of —
practice.solution: **Bhangra** is the men's dance and **Giddha** the women's — both Punjabi, tied to the Baisakhi harvest.

practice.q: The **Hojagiri** dance, famous for balancing on pots and bottles, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Hojagiri** — performed by Reang women of Tripura with astonishing balancing feats.

practice.q: **Nongkrem**, a thanksgiving folk dance, is performed by the Khasi community of —
practice.solution: **Nongkrem** — the Khasi harvest-thanksgiving dance of Meghalaya.

practice.q:
Match the North-East dances:
1. Cheraw — Mizoram
2. Hojagiri — Tripura
3. Nongkrem — Nagaland
Which are correct?
practice.solution: **Nongkrem** belongs to **Meghalaya** (Khasi), not Nagaland — Nagaland's famous festival is Hornbill.
practice.shortcut: Nongkrem is Khasi — Meghalaya, not Nagaland.

practice.q: The **Lavani** dance, performed to the beats of the dholki, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Lavani** grew inside the **tamasha** folk theatre of Maharashtra; the dholki drives its tempo.

practice.q: **Theyyam**, a ritual dance in which performers embody village deities, is practised in —
practice.solution: **Theyyam** — north Kerala's ritual art where (mostly male) performers are possessed by the goddess; not a classical dance.

practice.q: **Yakshagana**, the spectacular night-long dance-drama with huge headgear, comes from —
practice.solution: **Yakshagana** is Karnataka's folk dance-drama — the Keralite counterpart is Kathakali (a classical form).

practice.q: **Bihu**, danced during the Rongali festival in April, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Rongali (Bohag) Bihu** marks the Assamese new year and spring; the Bihu dance accompanies it.

practice.q: The **Karma** dance, worshipping the Karma tree, is common to the tribal belts of —
practice.solution: **Karma** — an adivasi dance of the Chhattisgarh-Jharkhand (and adjoining MP) belt, danced around a sal/Karma branch.

practice.q: Which of the following is **NOT** a folk dance of Rajasthan?
practice.solution: **Garba** is Gujarati; Ghoomar, Kalbelia and Chari are Rajasthani.
practice.shortcut: Garba crosses the border — it's Gujarat's.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Garba was inscribed on the UNESCO ICH list in 2023.
2. Kalbelia, Chhau and Mudiyettu were inscribed in 2010.
3. Yakshagana is recognised as a classical dance of India.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: **Yakshagana is a folk dance-drama** — not one of the recognised classical dances. The two ICH statements are correct.

practice.q: The **tabla** is classified as which type of instrument?
practice.solution: The tabla produces sound from a struck skin — an **avanaddha vadya**.

practice.q: Which of the following is a **wind** instrument?
practice.solution: **Nadaswaram** — the south Indian temple wind instrument, usually paired with the thavil drum.

practice.q: The **santoor**, once a Kashmiri folk instrument, is classed as —
practice.solution: The santoor has around **100 strings** struck with light mallets — a stringed instrument taken to the concert stage by Shivkumar Sharma.

practice.q: Ustad **Amjad Ali Khan** is a maestro of the —
practice.solution: **Amjad Ali Khan** — sarod; the senia-maihar lineage of his family is famous for it.

practice.q: **Pt. Shivkumar Sharma**, who took a Kashmiri folk instrument to the classical stage, played the —
practice.solution: **Shivkumar Sharma** = santoor; Hariprasad Chaurasia is the flute maestro of the same era.

practice.q: **Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt** won a Grammy (1994) for playing the —
practice.solution: His redesigned **slide guitar — the mohan veena** — won the 1994 Grammy with Ry Cooder for *A Meeting by the River*.

practice.q: Ustad **Allah Rakha**, doyen of the Punjab gharana, was a master of the —
practice.solution: **Allah Rakha** was the great tabla player — father and first teacher of **Zakir Hussain**.

practice.q: Who is called the **'Pitamaha (father) of Carnatic music'**?
practice.solution: **Purandara Dasa** systematised Carnatic teaching (sarali varisai onwards); the Trinity came after him.

practice.q: **Tansen**, one of the Navaratnas, adorned the court of —
practice.solution: **Tansen** — Akbar's court musician, the fountainhead of Hindustani music and the Miyan ki Malhar raga lore.

practice.q: Which raga-family statement is correct about **Hindustani** music?
options: Ragas are traditionally tied to times of the day
The violin is its lead instrument
practice.solution: Hindustani ragas carry time-of-day (and seasonal) associations; fixed kriti composition is the Carnatic hallmark.

practice.q: **Pt. Bhimsen Joshi**, Bharat Ratna 2008, was a vocalist of which gharana?
practice.solution: **Bhimsen Joshi** sang in the **Kirana** gharana line; the oldest khayal gharana is Gwalior.

practice.q: Which is regarded as the **oldest khayal gharana** of Hindustani music?
practice.solution: **Gwalior** gharana is the oldest of the khayal gharanas; Patiala is famous for Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

practice.q:
Arrange the musician **Bharat Ratnas** chronologically:
1. Ravi Shankar
2. M.S. Subbulakshmi
3. Lata Mangeshkar
4. Bhimsen Joshi
practice.solution: MS (1998) → Ravi Shankar (1999) → Lata + Bismillah (2001) → Bhimsen Joshi (2008).

practice.q: **Pattachitra**, scroll painting with Jagannath iconography, belongs mainly to —
practice.solution: **Pattachitra** — Odisha's cloth and palm-leaf painting tradition centred on Puri's Jagannath cult.

practice.q: **Gond** tribal painting is associated with —
practice.solution: **Gond** painting — the dot-and-line tribal art of the Gond community of central India (MP).

practice.q: **Thangka** paintings, used as devotional objects in monasteries, belong to the tradition of —
practice.solution: **Thangka** — consecrated cloth scrolls of Ladakh, Sikkim and the Tibetan Buddhist world.

practice.q: **Phad**, the painted narrative scroll of the Pabuji epic, is a tradition of —
practice.solution: **Phad** — Rajasthan's bhopa priests unroll the painted scroll while singing the Pabuji/Devnarayan epic.

practice.q: **Chikankari**, the shadow-work embroidery, is a craft of —
practice.solution: **Chikankari** — Lucknow's whitework embroidery, once associated with Mughal court dress.

practice.q: **Pochampally**, famous for ikat weave with GI status, is in —
practice.solution: **Pochampally ikat** — the Telangana village whose tie-and-dye weave carries a GI tag.

practice.q: **Channapatna**, known for lacquered wooden toys, lies in —
practice.solution: **Channapatna** (Ramanagara district, Karnataka) — 'toy town' with a GI-tagged lacquer-ware tradition.

practice.q: The name **Kalamkari** literally refers to —
practice.solution: **Kalam** = pen: the Srikalahasti style is hand-drawn with a bamboo pen; the Machilipatnam style uses block prints.

practice.q: **Pichwai** paintings, made as backdrops for the deity Srinathji, belong to —
practice.solution: **Pichwai** — Nathdwara's painted curtains/backdrops behind the idol of Srinathji (Krishna).

practice.q: Mughal painting is said to have **peaked under Jahangir**; it was **founded** under —
practice.solution: Akbar founded the imperial atelier (the *Hamzanama*); Jahangir's reign brought portraiture and naturalism to their peak. (Humayun did bring the Persian masters, but the workshop flourished under Akbar.)

practice.q: The painting ***Bharat Mata* (1905)**, icon of the Swadeshi era, was painted by —
practice.solution: **Abanindranath Tagore** — founder of the Bengal School; Nandalal Bose carried the school forward.

practice.q: **Raja Ravi Varma**, famed for realistic depictions of Indian subjects, worked mainly in —
practice.solution: The Kerala painter fused European academic realism with Indian themes; his press made his gods and heroines mass-market lithographs.

practice.q: Towering **gopurams** are a characteristic feature of which temple architecture?
practice.solution: **Gopurams** — the colossal gateway towers of south Indian (Dravida) temples, e.g. Meenakshi, Srirangam.

practice.q: **Vesara**, the hybrid temple style mixing Nagara and Dravida elements, flourished under —
practice.solution: **Vesara** — the Deccan style of the Chalukyas (Pattadakal, Badami) perfected by the Hoysalas (Belur, Halebidu).

practice.q: The **Lingaraja temple** at Bhubaneswar follows which style?
practice.solution: Odisha's temples (Lingaraja, Konark, Jagannath Puri) follow the **Kalinga** — an eastern branch of the Nagara style with deul towers.

practice.q: The **Brihadeeswara temple** at Thanjavur was built by —
practice.solution: **Rajaraja I** raised the Chola's Rajrajeswara temple around 1010 CE; his son Rajendra I built Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

practice.q: The **Chennakesava temple at Belur** was commissioned by the Hoysala king —
practice.solution: **Vishnuvardhana** built Belur's Chennakesava (c. 1117); Halebidu and Somanathapura complete the Hoysala trio.

practice.q: The **Sun Temple at Modhera** (Gujarat) was built by —
options: Bhima I of the Solanki dynasty
practice.solution: **Bhima I** (Chaulukya-Solanki) built Modhera; the Konark Sun Temple belongs to Narasimhadeva I — don't swap the two sun temples.

practice.q: The **Dilwara Jain temples** at Mount Abu were built during the reign of the —
practice.solution: The marble Jain temples — Vimal Vasahi built by minister Vimal Shah under **Bhima I's Solanki rule**.

practice.q: The **Ajanta caves**, famous for frescoes like the Bodhisattva Padmapani, are devoted to —
practice.solution: **Ajanta** — purely Buddhist, in two phases (Satavahana, then Vakataka 5th century); painting is its glory.

practice.q: **Elephanta caves**, with the great Maheshmurti of Shiva, lie near —
practice.solution: **Elephanta** — the island caves in Mumbai harbour; a mid-first-millennium rock-cut Shiva complex (UNESCO 1987).

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Ellora's Kailasa temple was carved top-down from one rock.
2. Ajanta's caves were made in two distinct phases.
3. Ellora has only Buddhist caves.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Ellora includes **Hindu, Buddhist and Jain** caves — statement 3 fails. The top-down Kailasa cut and Ajanta's Satavahana + Vakataka phases are correct.
practice.shortcut: Ellora is three-religion — 3 is the false one.

practice.q: In Buddhist architecture, the **chaitya** was the —
practice.solution: **Chaitya** = congregational prayer hall (apse-ended, pillared); **vihara** = the monks' monastery.

practice.q: The ribbed stone **amalaka** crowns the shikhara of which temples?
practice.solution: The **amalaka** — a ribbed, myrobalan-shaped cap topped by a kalasha — sits on the northern shikhara.

practice.q:
Match:
1. Konark — Narasimhadeva I
2. Gangaikonda Cholapuram — Rajendra I
3. Meenakshi gopurams — Nayak rulers
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three correct: Konark (Eastern Ganga), the Chola's second capital temple (Rajendra I), and Madurai's towering gopurams rebuilt by the Nayaks.

practice.q: **Onam**, celebrating King Mahabali's annual homecoming, is the harvest festival of —
practice.solution: **Onam** — Kerala's Chingam-month festival with pookalam flower carpets and the Vallam Kali snake-boat races.

practice.q: The **Hornbill Festival**, the 'festival of festivals', is held every December in —
practice.solution: **Hornbill** — 1–10 December at Kisama near Kohima, showcasing all Nagaland tribes.

practice.q: **Losar**, the new-year festival, is celebrated mainly in —
practice.solution: **Losar** — the Tibetan Buddhist new year of the trans-Himalayan belt.

practice.q: **Sarhul**, the spring festival worshipping the sal tree, belongs to the tribal culture of —
practice.solution: **Sarhul** — Jharkhand's adivasi spring festival centred on the sal tree and nature worship.

practice.q: **Wangala**, the hundred-drum harvest festival, is celebrated by the **Garo** community of —
practice.solution: **Wangala** — the Garos of Meghalaya thank the sun god Misi Sal after harvest.

practice.q: The **Kumbh Mela** does NOT rotate through which city?
practice.solution: The four Kumbh venues: **Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, Nashik** — Varanasi is not one.

practice.q: The **Sonepur fair**, one of Asia's largest cattle fairs, is held in —
practice.solution: **Sonepur** (near Patna) — at the Gandak-Ganga confluence; Pushkar in Rajasthan is the camel fair, Sonepur the elephant-cattle fair.

practice.q: **Jallikattu**, the bull-embracing sport, is associated with which festival?
practice.solution: **Jallikattu** — Tamil Nadu's bull sport during the Pongal season (Mattu Pongal).

practice.q:
Arrange by calendar:
1. Baisakhi
2. Pongal
3. Onam
4. Rongali Bihu
Which order is correct?
practice.solution: Pongal (mid-Jan) → Baisakhi (mid-Apr) → Rongali Bihu (mid-Apr, days after Baisakhi) → Onam (Aug–Sep).

practice.q: **Durga Puja** of Kolkata entered the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in —
practice.solution: **Durga Puja in Kolkata** — inscribed in **2021**; Garba followed in 2023.

practice.q: **Ramman**, the ritual festival-theatre of Garhwal on the UNESCO ICH list, belongs to —
practice.solution: **Ramman** — the Salur-dun village ritual of Garhwal, **Uttarakhand**, inscribed in **2009**.

practice.q:
Match the ICH inscriptions:
1. Yoga — 2016
2. Kumbh Mela — 2017
3. Sankirtana — Manipur, 2013
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three are right: Yoga (2016), Kumbh Mela (2017), and Manipur's **Sankirtana** (2013).

practice.q: **Dholavira**, the Harappan city inscribed as a UNESCO WHS in 2021, is in —
practice.solution: **Dholavira** (Rann of Kachchh, Gujarat) — 2021's second Indian inscription with Ramappa.

practice.q: **Santiniketan**, Rabindranath Tagore's university town, was inscribed as a UNESCO WHS in —
practice.solution: **Santiniketan** (West Bengal) — inscribed in **2023**, the same year as the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas.

practice.q: The **Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas** (Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura) are located in —
practice.solution: The Hoysala temples — Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura — all in **Karnataka**, inscribed in 2023.

practice.q:
Arrange the recent Indian WHS inscriptions:
1. Santiniketan
2. Ramappa temple
3. Moidams of Assam
4. Dholavira
practice.solution: Ramappa + Dholavira (2021) → Santiniketan (2023) → Moidams (2024).

practice.q: The **Sangeet Natak Akademi**, India's national academy of performing arts, was set up in —
practice.solution: **SNA 1953** — a year before the Sahitya (1954) and Lalit Kala (1954) Akademis.

practice.q: The **Film and Television Institute of India (FTII)** is located at —
practice.solution: **FTII (1960)** — on the former Prabhat Studio campus in Pune.

practice.q: Which Akademi is concerned with **fine arts (painting, sculpture, graphics)**?
practice.solution: **Lalit Kala Akademi (1954)** = visual arts; Sahitya = literature; Sangeet Natak = music-dance-drama.

practice.q: Which of the following is a **natural** World Heritage Site of India?
practice.solution: **Kaziranga** (Assam, 1985) — with Manas, Keoladeo and Sundarbans in the natural list.

practice.q: **Keoladeo National Park**, a natural WHS famous for birds, is in —
practice.solution: **Keoladeo (Bharatpur), Rajasthan** — inscribed 1985; the Sundarbans bird-adjacent natural site is in Bengal.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Khangchendzonga National Park is India's only mixed WHS.
2. The Western Ghats are a natural WHS.
3. Manas National Park is a cultural WHS.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: **Manas is natural**, not cultural — Assam's pair (Kaziranga, Manas) is both natural.

practice.q: India's **first four** World Heritage Sites, inscribed in 1983, included —
options: Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora
practice.solution: The 1983 batch: **Taj Mahal, Agra Fort, Ajanta, Ellora**; Konark and Mahabalipuram followed in 1984.

practice.q: The **Archaeological Survey of India's** first Director-General was —
practice.solution: **Alexander Cunningham** — the 'father of Indian archaeology', first DG from 1861.

practice.q:
Match the inscriptions:
1. Ramappa temple — Telangana, 2021
2. Maratha Military Landscapes — 2025
3. Sarnath Buddhist site — 2026
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three: Ramappa (Telangana, 2021), the Maratha fort landscapes of Maharashtra-Tamil Nadu (2025), and Sarnath (2026) — India's most recent inscriptions.
